name: Masco Corporation
executive_summary: Masco Corporation is a branded home-improvement compounder—BEHR coatings, DELTA/HANSGROHE plumbing, LIBERTY hardware—tilted to repair-and-remodel rather than new-build exposure. The quantitative screen flags a **strong buy** (9/22 models; composite 83%; P/E 19.6; 1.6% yield), supported by earnings quality, dividend growth, and sustained buybacks. Filings show a volume-soft top line but improving earnings per share via pricing, cost actions, and repurchases; Q1 2026 was the clearest inflection (+6% sales to $1,918m; diluted EPS $1.05 vs $0.87). The central debate is whether plumbing pricing power and capital return offset housing-cycle risk, tariff pressure, and Decorative Architectural weakness—especially given ~38% sales concentration with The Home Depot and negative common shareholders’ equity from years of buybacks (which distorts P/B and ROE screen inputs).
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Masco offers **quality at a reasonable earnings multiple**, not a classic asset bargain. The screen passes five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with standouts including Graham Enterprising, Lynch/Neff PEG variants, Buffett Quality, Magic Formula, and Earnings Quality. That profile fits a cash-generative franchise trading below ~20x earnings while returning capital systematically.

Business quality is credible in the primary filings. The FY2025 10-K describes category-leading brands, a focused two-segment portfolio (Plumbing Products; Decorative Architectural Products), and a capital-allocation framework prioritising reinvestment, investment-grade credit, dividends, and excess free cash to repurchases. FY2025 net income was $810m (diluted EPS $3.86, +3% YoY) on net sales of $7,562m (-3%), with Plumbing +3% to $4,992m partly offsetting Decorative -14% to $2,570m (including the Kichler divestiture). Share count fell materially (8.5m shares repurchased for ~$576m; new $2.0bn authorisation in February 2026).

The screen’s **strong buy** signal aligns with this operating and capital-return story, but several caveats matter. P/B (-66.1) and ROE (84.6%) are not economically meaningful given negative common equity and large goodwill/intangibles. The screen failed FCF Yield, Financial Health, Deep Value, and Piotroski (6/9)—consistent with cyclical volume pressure, leverage, and margin compression. Conviction on the screen is only 52% (“new”, one week at signal). Deep research therefore supports the **earnings-and-quality** pillar of the case more than the **balance-sheet deep value** pillar.
financial_review:
*Primary source: SEC EDGAR filing body extracts. Where the cash-flow statement was truncated in the 10-K body, Yahoo fallback is noted.*

**Annual trend (10-K, year ended 31 December 2025 vs 2024)**

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Net sales | $7,562m | $7,828m | -3% |
| Net sales (ex-divestitures & FX) | $7,517m | $7,650m | -2% |
| Gross margin | 35.4% | 36.2% | -80 bps |
| Operating profit | $1,248m | $1,363m | -8% |
| Net income | $810m | $822m | -1% |
| Diluted EPS | $3.86 | $3.76 | +3% |

Volume drove the decline: lower sales volume cut consolidated sales ~4%, partly offset by plumbing price (+2%). Tariffs and commodity inflation weighed on gross margin; management cites tariff exposure “principally in our Plumbing Products segment, due to duties and tariffs related to China.” FY2024 (10-K filed February 2025) showed a similar pattern: net sales $7,828m (-2%), net income $822m (-9% vs 2023’s $908m), with the Kichler divestiture ($125m proceeds; ~$88m loss) and a softer Decorative segment.

**Interim trend (10-Q filings)**

*Q1 2026 (three months ended 31 March 2026 vs 2025):* Net sales $1,918m vs $1,801m; operating profit $316m vs $286m (+10%); net income attributable to Masco $213m vs $186m (+15%); diluted EPS $1.05 vs $0.87 (+21%). Management attributes growth primarily to higher net selling prices (+5%), partly offset by lower paint/coating volume (-1%). Segment net sales: Plumbing $1,364m; Decorative $554m. Liberty Hardware was reclassified into Plumbing from Q1 2026, affecting comparability.

*Q2 2025 (30 June):* Net sales $2,051m vs $2,091m; net income $270m vs $258m; diluted EPS $1.28 vs $1.17.

*Q3 2025 (30 September):* Net sales $1,917m vs $1,983m (-3%); net income $189m vs $167m; diluted EPS $0.90 vs $0.77. **Nine months ended 30 September 2025:** net sales $5,769m vs $6,000m (-4%); net income attributable to Masco $645m vs $640m (+1%); diluted EPS $3.06 vs $2.91 (+5%). Plumbing 9M sales +2%; Decorative -13%.

**Balance sheet and cash flow**

At 31 December 2025 (10-K): cash $647m; total debt ~$3.2bn; net debt ~$2.3bn; **total debt/total capitalisation 97%** (102% at end-2024). The 2022 credit agreement requires net leverage ≤4.0x and interest coverage ≥2.5x; Masco reported compliance with **no borrowings outstanding** on the $1.0bn revolver. Common stockholders’ equity was **negative** (~-$186m per Yahoo `financials_annual.json`; filing body truncated before the full balance sheet)—reflecting cumulative repurchases exceeding retained earnings, not operational insolvency.

Capital expenditure was $156m in FY2025 (guidance ~$190m for 2026). Dividends paid totalled $261m ($1.24/share; $1.28/share intended for 2026). **Operating and free cash flow:** the 10-K body extract does not include the full cash-flow statement; per **Yahoo fallback** (`financials_annual.json`), FY2025 operating cash flow was **$1,022m** and free cash flow **$866m** (FY2024 FCF $907m). Q1 2026 showed **net cash used in operations of $79m**, driven by working-capital seasonality (receivables +$308m).

**Gaps:** Eight 8-K filings in the index lack body extracts (including several 2026 events). Note R litigation detail is referenced in the 10-K but not present in the truncated body. No going-concern language was found.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and demand.** Filings repeatedly warn of “lower market demand,” tied to repair/remodel and (lesser) new-build activity—sensitive to consumer confidence, mortgage rates, and home-equity availability. Macro context (10-year Treasury ~4.7%) is a headwind for housing-related names but is not treated here as a veto of the screen signal.

**Customer concentration.** The Home Depot accounted for **~38% of FY2025 net sales (~$2.9bn)**. Behr brand retail exclusivity with Home Depot limits channel flexibility; loss of this customer would be “material.” Ferguson and Lowe’s are also named as significant customers.

**Tariffs and input costs.** FY2025 and interim filings flag “significantly higher costs… due to the recently enacted tariffs, particularly those related to China,” mainly in Plumbing. Management seeks mitigation via pricing, sourcing, and cost savings, but warns that price increases can erode volume and share.

**Margin and mix.** FY2025 gross margin fell 80 bps; operating margin 16.5% vs 17.4%. Decorative Architectural remains structurally weaker (FY2025 sales -14%; 9M 2025 -13%).

**Leverage and capital structure.** Debt/capitalisation near 97% and negative common equity increase financial risk if earnings contract. Credit-agreement covenants (net leverage ≤4.0x) are currently met, but the 10-K cautions that a severe earnings decline could constrain borrowing flexibility.

**Restructuring and leadership.** Q4 2025 restructuring charges ~$18m; **~$50m additional expected in 2026**. An 8-K (8 December 2025) announced departure of Group President Imran Ahmad (Decorative Architectural); CEO Jon Nudi assumed segment oversight—execution risk during reorganisation (Liberty integration into Plumbing from Q1 2026).

**Governance / litigation / other.** Extensive ordinary-course litigation risk is disclosed (product liability, environmental, employment, etc.); Note R detail unavailable in body extract. Cybersecurity, supplier dependence, and private-label competition at big-box retailers are further filing-highlighted risks. Pension/post-retirement obligations appear on the balance sheet but detailed funding status is not in the available extracts.

research_rationale: Filings confirm a high-quality, cash-return compounder at a reasonable earnings multiple with a genuine Q1 2026 operational inflection, partially validating the strong-buy screen, but cyclical volume risk, tariff pressure, Home Depot concentration, and negative equity/l everage metrics warrant a measured—not maximal—conviction overlay.
